name: Bank of England news RSS
why: BoE announcements and policy-related releases are immediate drivers of sterling repricing.

name: Bank of England speeches RSS
why: MPC tone and guidance changes often show up in speeches before the market fully reprices them.

name: Bank of England statistics RSS
why: Helpful for official releases that matter to rates and liquidity conditions in sterling markets.

name: Bank Rate latest decision page
cadence: Eight times a year plus updates
why: Current Bank Rate and the policy narrative are primary inputs for GBPJPY rate-differential thinking.

name: Bank of England MPC dates
why: Knowing when the next decision is due helps the swarm weight event risk and narrative urgency.

name: Bank of England database
why: Useful for series-level adapters such as official rates or market expectations.
notes: Discovery source; best used with explicit series selection.

name: ONS consumer price inflation bulletin
why: UK inflation surprises materially affect BoE pricing and sterling.

name: ONS CPI dataset page
why: Useful when you want the raw CPI tables behind the bulletin rather than the narrative summary.

name: ONS GDP monthly estimate
why: Growth data matters for the BoE path and for the relative attractiveness of sterling versus yen.

name: ONS labour market overview
why: Labor-market tightness is a core BoE input and therefore a GBPJPY driver.

name: ONS developer hub
why: Best source for adding structured UK macro time series once you promote the bridge beyond headline scraping.

name: Bank of Japan English what's new RSS
why: English-language BoJ updates are the easiest official feed for policy-sensitive yen developments.

name: Bank of Japan Japanese what's new RSS
why: Japanese feed can surface updates with less translation lag than the English site.

name: BoJ monetary policy releases 2026 page
why: Direct BoJ policy statements are indispensable for yen direction and intervention risk framing.

name: BoJ daily foreign exchange rates
why: Provides official reference rates and a useful sanity check on recent yen moves.

name: Japan CPI release schedule
why: Event calendar context helps the swarm weight imminent JPY volatility around CPI.

name: Japan labour force release schedule
why: Useful for anticipating JPY-sensitive labor releases and avoiding stale economic context.

name: e-Stat what's new
provider: Portal Site of Official Statistics of Japan
why: Useful release monitor for new and updated Japanese official statistics.

name: e-Stat API specification
provider: Portal Site of Official Statistics of Japan
why: Structured Japanese macro data source once you add series-aware API adapters.

name: Japan Ministry of Finance FX intervention monthly release
why: Critical for GBPJPY because yen intervention risk can overwhelm otherwise clean rate-differential trades.

name: CFTC Commitments of Traders
why: Leveraged-fund and asset-manager positioning is useful for spotting crowded GBP or JPY directional trades.

name: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report
why: The WPSR is the anchor public inventory release for WTI, especially crude, gasoline, distillates and refinery utilization.

name: EIA Today in Energy RSS
why: Timely official energy-market analysis is useful context for inventories, demand and infrastructure trends.

name: EIA press releases RSS
why: Captures official announcements, outlook changes and methodology notes that can reset market expectations.

name: EIA gasoline and diesel RSS
why: Downstream pricing and crack-spread context help the swarm reason about refinery demand and product tightness.

name: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook
why: The STEO provides official demand, supply and price outlook revisions that shape the medium-term oil narrative.

name: EIA API documentation
why: Best source for structured inventory, production and refinery data once you add series-specific adapters.

name: EIA open data browser
why: Helpful for discovering the exact series you want to bind into the oil context pipeline.
notes: Treat this as a discovery source, not a direct headline feed.

name: CFTC Commitments of Traders
why: Positioning helps detect crowded oil trades and whether inventory reactions may extend or mean revert.

name: NOAA National Hurricane Center tropical weather outlook RSS
why: Storm threats can materially affect Gulf production, refining and shipping infrastructure.

name: NOAA NHC Atlantic outlook RSS
why: Adds Atlantic storm bulletins and updates that often matter for oil more than broad macro headlines do.

name: OPEC Monthly Oil Market Report
why: OPEC demand, supply and balance revisions shape the global oil narrative and can move front-month crude.
notes: Valuable but not ideal for the auto-fetch path because the site and downloadable artifacts are less scrape-friendly.

name: IEA Oil Market Report
why: A high-signal global oil balance source, especially for demand revisions and inventory interpretation.
notes: Paid and delayed; include manually if you have access, otherwise use public release metadata only.

name: MINING.com oil sands RSS
why: Useful for Canada-heavy supply and infrastructure headlines that can bleed into North American crude narratives.

name: Federal Reserve press releases RSS
why: High-impact FOMC, emergency facilities and policy communications move real-rate expectations, the US dollar and gold.

name: Federal Reserve speeches and testimony RSS
why: Policy tone shifts often appear first in speeches, testimonies and prepared remarks.

name: BLS CPI RSS
why: US inflation surprises reprice Fed expectations and real yields, which are core gold drivers.

name: BLS Employment Situation release page
why: Payrolls and unemployment data directly affect rate-path pricing, USD direction and gold sentiment.

name: BEA Personal Income and PCE page
why: PCE inflation and spending are core macro inputs for Fed pricing and therefore for gold.

name: CME FedWatch
why: Exchange-implied probability shifts are often a cleaner signal than headlines alone.
notes: JS-heavy page; best scraped via a dedicated adapter or manual summary.

name: CFTC Commitments of Traders
why: Managed-money and hedger positioning helps the swarm detect crowded gold trades and squeeze risk.

name: World Gold Council ETF holdings and flows
why: ETF flow data is one of the cleanest publicly available demand measures for gold.

name: World Gold Council trading volumes
why: Liquidity and turnover context help distinguish genuine regime shifts from thin-market noise.

name: World Gold Council central-bank reserves
why: Official-sector accumulation supports medium-term gold demand narratives and reserve-diversification themes.

name: LBMA daily trade reporting data
why: London bullion market turnover helps detect whether a move is backed by deeper spot-market participation.

name: Bank of England gold statistics
why: BoE custody holdings give another official-sector lens on bullion stock changes and vault demand.

name: MINING.com gold RSS
why: Useful for supply-side headlines, miners, M&A, disruptions and gold-market specific narrative color.

name: FRED API documentation
provider: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
why: Useful for adding structured real-rate, DXY, breakeven or financial-condition series to the context builder.
notes: Best used with preselected series IDs rather than raw endpoint discovery.
